investigations.name: Critical business service review
investigations.description: Sit with the service owners and establish what the business actually cannot lose, and what each service depends on.
investigations.workingNarrative: Your architecture lead is working through the service owners one by one.

investigations.name: Architecture and dependency review
investigations.description: Map what actually connects to what, rather than what the diagrams say.
investigations.workingNarrative: The architecture team is reconciling three different network diagrams against reality.

investigations.name: Privileged access review
investigations.description: Establish who actually holds administrative rights, including accounts that do not belong to employees.
investigations.workingNarrative: The IAM team is pulling every privileged group membership and matching it against HR records.

investigations.name: Supplier access review
investigations.description: Establish what each major supplier can reach, with which accounts, and who watches them.
investigations.workingNarrative: Cyber risk is working through supplier contracts and the access they actually rely on.

investigations.name: Targeted threat hunt
investigations.description: Hunt for signs that someone is already inside, focused on privileged identity and remote access.
investigations.workingNarrative: The SOC team is hunting through what telemetry exists for evidence of activity nobody has explained.

investigations.name: Recovery test for a critical service
investigations.description: Attempt a full restore of a critical service and time it honestly.
investigations.workingNarrative: Engineering is running a restore in a clean environment. Operations is watching nervously.

investigations.name: Control effectiveness testing
investigations.description: Test whether the controls the organisation believes it has are actually operating.
investigations.workingNarrative: Cyber risk is testing controls rather than reading control descriptions.

investigations.name: Vulnerability triage by exposure
investigations.description: Re-cut the vulnerability backlog by what is actually reachable and what it would reach.
investigations.workingNarrative: Security engineering is cross-referencing findings against exposure rather than severity.

investigations.name: Cloud configuration review
investigations.description: Review the production and non-production tenancies against a baseline worth having.
investigations.workingNarrative: The architecture team is working through cloud configuration with the platform engineers.

investigations.name: Data holdings and access review
investigations.description: Establish what data Nexora holds, where, and who can read it.
investigations.workingNarrative: Cyber risk and Legal are working through data holdings together.

investigations.name: Legacy estate inventory
investigations.description: Find out what is actually still running in the legacy data centre.
investigations.workingNarrative: Two engineers are physically walking the legacy estate with a clipboard and a scanner.

investigations.name: Commission a penetration test
investigations.description: Pay someone to walk the paths you suspect exist.
investigations.workingNarrative: The testers are in. Nobody in infrastructure is enjoying it.

investigations.name: Incident response readiness review
investigations.description: Establish whether the organisation could actually run an incident.
investigations.workingNarrative: Your SOC lead is walking the response plan against a realistic scenario.

investigations.name: Cyber team capability review
investigations.description: Understand what your own team can actually sustain.
investigations.workingNarrative: You are spending time with each function lead rather than reading their reports.

investigations.name: Sector threat intelligence review
investigations.description: Find out what is actually happening to organisations like this one.
investigations.workingNarrative: Cyber risk is reading sector reporting rather than generic threat feeds.

investigations.name: Technical due diligence on the acquisition
investigations.description: Examine Kestrel Digital's estate before it is connected to Nexora's.
investigations.workingNarrative: Two of your people are on site at Kestrel with a very short list of questions.

investigations.name: Review the inherited risk register
investigations.description: Work out which of the 23 inherited entries describe anything that is still true.
investigations.workingNarrative: Cyber risk is testing each inherited entry against current evidence.

investigations.name: Check exposure to the HR provider incident
investigations.description: Establish whether People Cloud's incident touched Nexora's employee data.
investigations.workingNarrative: Cyber risk is pressing the provider for specifics rather than reassurance.

glossary.definition: An observation about the organisation. A finding, an alert, a test result or something someone told you. Evidence is not a risk until you interpret it.
glossary.guidedNote: Collect evidence, then decide what it means. The two are different jobs.

glossary.definition: A proposition about how harm could occur, which evidence can support or contradict. Hypotheses are meant to be tested, not defended.
glossary.guidedNote: Forming a hypothesis costs you attention. Choose which ones are worth testing.

glossary.definition: Threat, pathway and business consequence stated together. 'Unpatched server' is not a scenario; 'an actor reaches fulfilment through an unpatched server and stops despatch for a day' is.
glossary.guidedNote: A scenario the business can picture is a scenario the business can decide about.

glossary.definition: What remains after the controls that actually operate, rather than the controls that exist on paper.
glossary.guidedNote: Bands, not numbers. The precision would be false.

glossary.definition: Something a decision depends on being true. When the world changes, assumptions can quietly stop being true without anyone revisiting the decision.
glossary.guidedNote: Record assumptions when you accept risk. The game will tell you when one fails.

glossary.definition: Coverage, configuration quality, operating effectiveness and exceptions taken together. A control that covers 40% of the estate is a 40% control.
glossary.guidedNote: 'We have MFA' is a statement about procurement, not about security.

glossary.definition: The sequence of steps an actor would take from where they start to what they want. Controls sit on specific steps.
glossary.guidedNote: Breaking one step can be worth more than improving five controls.

glossary.definition: How long an actor operates inside the environment before anyone notices.
glossary.guidedNote: Detection coverage and dwell time are the same conversation.

glossary.definition: Your own week. Every intervention, review and meeting costs some of it, and it does not carry over.
glossary.guidedNote: Attention is the scarcest resource you have, and the easiest to waste.

glossary.definition: What your functions can actually deliver. Committing beyond capacity does not produce more work; it produces worse work, later.
glossary.guidedNote: An overloaded team returns thinner investigations and misses more.

glossary.definition: Assigning work to a leader. Their skill, workload and morale shape both the quality and the timeliness of what comes back.
glossary.guidedNote: You cannot do everything yourself, and who you ask matters.

glossary.definition: A long-running investment that improves controls gradually. Programmes take months, hit blockers and compete for the same people.
Whether an executive will act on your advice. Built by understanding their priorities and spent by asking for things.
glossary.guidedNote: Escalating everything is how influence is lost.

glossary.definition: How much friction, downtime and process the business will currently absorb for security reasons.
glossary.guidedNote: Spend it deliberately. It recovers slowly.

glossary.definition: Severe-looking findings that do not matter, and moderate findings that do. Volume is not risk.
glossary.guidedNote: A critical vulnerability on an isolated test system matters less than a moderate weakness in identity.

glossary.definition: Several important services leaning on the same platform, identity or supplier, so one failure becomes many.
glossary.guidedNote: Concentration turns an incident into a crisis.

glossary.definition: The post-incident view of the path taken, what helped, what hurt, and which earlier decisions shaped the outcome.
glossary.guidedNote: Not a verdict on whether you were right. A record of what mattered.

glossary.definition: How much of a risk assessment rests on things you have actually verified rather than inherited.
glossary.guidedNote: Communicating uncertainty honestly is a skill boards value.

glossary.definition: The value that determines this world's hidden configuration. The same seed always produces the same Nexora.
glossary.guidedNote: Share a seed to compare how differently two people play the same organisation.

glossary.definition: Security operations centre: the team, in-house or contracted, that watches alerts around the clock and decides which ones to escalate. Nexora's is a contracted service.
Multi-factor authentication: proving who you are with something beyond a password, such as a code on a phone. An account without it falls to a stolen password alone.
Accounts that can change how systems work, not just use them: administrators, service accounts, engineers with production rights. Most attack paths run through one.
Anything that proves identity to a system: a password, a token, a key. Stolen credentials let an attacker walk in as somebody who belongs.
An account used by software rather than a person. They rarely have a second factor, rarely change their password, and often nobody owns them.
Dividing a network so that reaching one part does not mean reaching all of it. Where it is missing, one compromised machine can route to everything.
A direct network link between two environments, such as a test environment and production. It is convenient, and it makes the weaker one a path into the stronger.
Nexora's own slice of a cloud provider: the accounts, storage and workloads it runs there. Publicly readable storage in the production tenancy is data left in the street.
The automated route by which code becomes a running system. If it holds standing production credentials, compromising an engineer or a repository compromises production.
The identity a running program uses to reach other systems. Over-permissioned, it lets a compromised application read far more than it needs.
A hardened machine administrators go through to reach production. Everything behind it depends on how well it is controlled.
A system that holds administrative credentials and hands them out for a session, recording who took what. Privileged access management is the practice around it.
An emergency route to privileged access that is normally closed: requested, time-limited and recorded. The alternative is permanent standing access nobody watches.
How staff and suppliers reach the internal network from outside. Out-of-hours use of a vendor's remote access is worth a question.
A laptop, workstation or server. Endpoint detection and response is the software that watches what runs on it and can stop or isolate it.
The record of what systems did: who logged in, what ran, what connected where. Where it is missing, an intrusion can reach business impact unseen.
A patch fixes a known weakness in software. An exploit is working code that uses that weakness. Once an exploit is published, the time to patch is measured in days.
A message crafted to make somebody hand over a credential or run something. Targeted at finance or executives it is the commonest way in.
An attack that encrypts systems and demands payment for the key. What decides the outcome is whether recovery works without paying.
A backup copy that cannot be altered or deleted for a set period, even by an administrator. Backups sharing credentials with production are the opposite.
The two halves of responding to an incident: stopping the attacker's access, then restoring the services affected. They are scored separately because they fail separately.
A contract with a specialist firm agreed before an incident, so help arrives on a known footing. Without one, expert support is bought at emergency rates in the middle of the night.
Watching what data leaves. Without it, a slow theft can stay below every alert threshold for months.
The overall state of an organisation's defences at a point in time. It drifts downward on its own unless something maintains it.
Evidence that a control works, as opposed to a statement that it exists. A supplier questionnaire returned clean is a statement; a test is assurance.

Payment card details, the industry standard that governs how they are handled, and the bank that processes Nexora's card payments and can stop doing so. Card data found outside the defined payment environment is both a compliance question and a risk question.
Systems Nexora's partners log into from outside. If partner accounts live in the same directory as staff accounts, a partner's stolen password starts inside the staff boundary.
A supplier that runs part of Nexora's technology on its behalf, and holds the access to do so. Its engineers' standing administrative accounts are Nexora's exposure, not the supplier's.
